headline_en: Higher study opportunities in Austria, with scholarships for bachelor's and PhD
summary_en: A detailed guide (credited to UNB) to studying in Austria for Bangladeshi students: admission requirements and intakes, the two-stage residence-permit and D-visa process through the Austrian Embassy in New Delhi, required documents and proof of funds, visa fee and timing, tuition and living costs, scholarships, part-time work rules and post-study permits.

facts.statement: At Austrian public universities study is free only for local students; foreign students proficient in German get a substantial discount on study costs. English proficiency is accepted as an alternative to German, especially for international students.
QS rankings stated: University of Vienna 137, Technical University of Vienna 190, Graz University of Technology 413, Johannes Kepler University Linz 472.

Admission requirements: a diploma or high-school certificate for a bachelor's degree; a bachelor's in the same or a relevant subject for postgraduate courses; relevant professional experience is a precondition for bachelor's degrees at universities of applied sciences; a master's programme requires at least 180 ECTS credits and a relevant bachelor's degree of at least six semesters; PhD programmes require a master's degree with research or equivalent study in the relevant field.

Austrian institutions admit students in two intakes: the winter semester starting in September and the summer semester starting in February; registration periods vary by course and are updated on each institution's website, and the whole application is done through the institution's online portal with document uploads.

Documents usually needed for admission: passport and photo or a government-issued ID copy; latest diploma/high-school or bachelor's certificate; relevant professional experience for applied-science bachelor's; English proficiency proof (IELTS, PTE Academic, TOEFL or Cambridge certificate); German proficiency proof for German-taught courses; plus anything else the institution asks for.

Some Austrian universities, especially at bachelor's level, hold an entrance exam, usually six months before the programme starts; at other levels students are assessed by online oral exam or interview (Zoom or Skype). Hand-filled papers may need to be sent by post as well as email; results and instructions come by email.
Once admission is confirmed the student is asked to pay the study fee; the offer letter and student ID are issued only after this fee is paid.

For long-term study Bangladeshi students must apply for a D-type visa, which permits a stay of more than six months. The visa should be applied for at least three to six months before classes start; the applicant should apply at least three months before entering Austria because the final decision takes time.

The process has two stages: first an application for a residence permit, then for an entry permit. The first stage is completed at the Austrian Embassy in New Delhi, India (address: EP-13, Chandragupta Marg, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi 110021, India). An appointment must be taken by email before going; on the date given in the reply the applicant attends with all papers and gives biometric data (fingerprints and photograph). The embassy sends the application directly to Austria, where the residence permit is processed.

When Austria informs the embassy that the residence permit is granted, the embassy notifies the applicant, who must apply for entry within three months of that notice; the embassy then issues a D-type visa to enter Austria, and the applicant must reach Austria and collect the residence permit within a further three months.

Documents for the Austrian student visa, with a hand-filled and signed application form: a valid passport with at least two blank pages, valid for at least three months from the day of arrival in Austria; two recent passport-size photos; offer letter from the Austrian institution; proof of sufficient funds; health insurance covering emergency treatment and travel; proof of advance accommodation in Austria. Originals plus one set of copies; any document in Bangla must be submitted with a certified German translation.
Proof of funds for the Austrian student visa: at least 6,630 euros must be shown as the minimum cost for one year. The health insurance required typically costs about 69.13 euros per month.

The overall processing cost from application until receiving the Austrian visa is 120 euros. Processing usually takes about 15 working days, but can extend to 30 to 60 working days if additional documents are needed.

Tuition: foreign students at Austrian public universities pay on average 1,452 euros a year; universities of applied sciences can cost 727 to 7,500 euros per semester; private universities usually 3,000 to 23,000 euros a year, up to 35,000 euros for some business programmes.

Living costs: a monthly budget of 900 to 1,300 euros in cities like Vienna and Salzburg (housing, food, social activities, public transport included); 900 to 1,000 euros a month in cities like Linz or Graz.

Scholarships listed: Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide (for 'graduate programme or PhD' as printed) with a monthly stipend of 1,150 euros plus up to 1,000 euros of travel cost against travel receipts; Erasmus Mundus programmes covering full tuition, visa costs, travel, insurance and monthly allowance, about 12,000 euros in all; OeAD Housing Scholarship up to 6,000 euros; University of Vienna scholarship of 12,000 euros; Joint Japan World Bank Graduate Scholarship (tuition, monthly stipend, round-trip airfare, health insurance); Austrian Development Cooperation scholarship; and the Helmut Veith Stipend for Women in Computer Science (tuition, monthly stipend).

Foreign students in Austria may do part-time jobs but need a work permit (not needed for business or freelancing). To get it they need a job offer from an Austrian business and must show the job offer letter with their residence permit. The work permit is renewable, valid one year, and allows at most 20 hours of work per week.

After graduating there are two permits for staying in Austria: a residence permit for job seekers, and the Red-White-Red Card for graduates to stay and work full time. The article says both allow graduates to work for up to one year. The job-seeker permit must be applied for before the student residence permit expires and allows at most 20 hours' work a week; the Red-White-Red Card is applied for after getting a job offer, the decision takes 15 days, and it allows up to 40 hours a week.

To cut living costs the article suggests sharing an apartment outside the city with other students (rents much lower than the centre, though far from the university), using public transport, and using the university student card, which gives notable discounts on public and private services.

headline_en: Documents attested by the Foreign Ministry will not need re-attestation in other countries: Hasan Mahmud
summary_en: On Monday 29 July 2024 in The Hague, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud handed over Bangladesh's instrument of accession to the 1961 Apostille Convention. The ministry said documents attested by the Foreign Ministry would no longer need re-attestation abroad, that electronic apostille certificates with QR codes would be issued, and that Bangladeshis going abroad would save 500 to 600 crore taka a year; the e-APP was expected to be fully running within eight months.

facts.statement: Bangladesh was made a party to the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention, 1961) at a ceremony at the Dutch Foreign Ministry in The Hague, where Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud handed over the instrument of accession. The Foreign Ministry said documents attested by Bangladesh's Foreign Ministry would 'from now on' not need to be attested again in other countries.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud / Foreign Ministry press release, 29 July 2024

facts.statement: The Foreign Ministry said the change would save Bangladeshis going abroad 500 to 600 crore taka every year.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud / Foreign Ministry press release, 29 July 2024

facts.statement: Under the e-APP (Electronic Apostille Programme) documents will be attested and an electronic apostille certificate issued, whose authenticity can be verified from anywhere in the world using the QR code on the certificate.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud / Foreign Ministry press release, 29 July 2024

facts.statement: The minister hoped that, as for other countries, the e-APP could be fully launched for Bangladeshi citizens within eight months of accession, with the final support of the other states party to the convention (so it was not yet fully operating in July 2024).
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud / Foreign Ministry press release, 29 July 2024

facts.statement: Before the change: documents such as academic certificates, birth registration certificates and marriage certificates, needed for study abroad, job applications, settling abroad or marrying a foreign national, had to be attested by several Bangladeshi ministries and the Foreign Ministry, and then again by the foreign embassy, the destination country's foreign ministry and other foreign authorities, which was time-consuming, laborious and costly.

headline_en: 5 Bangladeshis killed in Dubai: 'Bring my Raju back, let me see his face once'
summary_en: Five Bangladeshi workers employed by the same firm were killed on the spot when their vehicle exploded on the way to work in Dubai at about 7:30 am local time on Sunday 7 July 2024. Four were from Balenga village in Nawabganj upazila, Dhaka, and one from Dohar; the report describes the grieving families and the debts taken to send the men abroad.

facts.statement: Five Bangladeshis were killed on the spot when a vehicle exploded while they were going to their workplace in Dubai at about 7:30 am local time on Sunday 7 July 2024; all five worked at the same establishment. Four were from Balenga village, Joykrishnapur union, Nawabganj upazila, Dhaka, and one from the Dohar Bazar area of Dohar upazila.

The dead were: Md. Rana (30), son of Lutfor Rahman; Md. Rashed (32), son of Abdul Hakim; Md. Raju (24), son of Sheikh Irshad; Ibadul Islam (34), son of Sheikh Ibrahim, all of Balenga village; and Md. Hira Mia (22), son of Md. Manjur, of Dohar Bazar.
Ibadul Islam's mother Nazma Begum took 1.5 lakh taka from an NGO a year before to send her son to Dubai; she said she must still bear the instalments although he has died.
facts.source_in_article: Nazma Begum, mother of the deceased

facts.statement: Md. Rashed's mother Yaron Begum sent him abroad on borrowed money and the debt had not yet been repaid when he died; he was the family's only earner.
The families appealed for the bodies to be brought home; the article reports no information on repatriation of the bodies, the employer's name or compensation.

It was a proposal, not yet an agreement.

headline_en: Saudi investment in Bangladesh took priority
summary_en: At the Bangladesh-Saudi political dialogue in Riyadh on 1 July 2024, led by foreign ministers Hasan Mahmud and Prince Faisal bin Farhan, investment in Bangladesh dominated. On labour, the two sides discussed forming a joint task force to bring transparency to manpower export to Saudi Arabia and stop worker harassment by vested interests, and Bangladesh asked for a special registration opportunity for expatriates doing business there.

facts.statement: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud thanked Saudi Arabia for giving employment opportunities to 3 million (30 lakh) Bangladeshis.

At the Riyadh political dialogue the two sides had 'fruitful discussion' on forming a joint task force to bring more transparency to Bangladeshi manpower export to Saudi Arabia and to stop harassment of workers by vested quarters; the article reports discussion, not a formed task force.
Hasan Mahmud requested the Saudi foreign minister to give a special opportunity for registration to expatriate Bangladeshis doing business in Saudi Arabia.

The dialogue decided to adopt a joint work plan to celebrate the golden jubilee of Saudi-Bangladesh diplomatic relations the following year (2025) and to upgrade the Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia Joint Commission meeting to ministerial level.

headline_en: Crowd catches SI while robbing gold from Saudi-returned expatriate
summary_en: On Sunday 19 May 2024 in Chattogram, an off-duty police sub-inspector of Khulshi police station and two associates stopped the car of a Saudi-returned expatriate coming from Shah Amanat International Airport and took 16 bhori of gold from him. Bystanders caught the SI and one associate on a flyover; the SI was suspended and a case was being filed.

facts.statement: At about 3 pm on Sunday 19 May 2024, Saudi expatriate Abdul Khalek (also printed as Mohammad Khalek) was returning from Chattogram Shah Amanat International Airport when his vehicle was stopped at Khulshi Tiger Pass by Sub-Inspector Aminul Islam of Khulshi police station with two associates, who snatched 16 bhori of gold from him, drove him around the city in the vehicle and tried to drop him off on the Akhtaruzzaman Chowdhury flyover.
facts.source_in_article: Panchlaish police station OC Santosh Kumar Chakma

facts.statement: The expatriate held on to the officer's clothes, a crowd gathered and Panchlaish police detained SI Aminul Islam and associate Shahidul Islam Jahed (45) of KB Aman Ali Road, Rahattar Pool, Bakalia; a third man fled. The SI, who was not on duty, was temporarily suspended and a case was being filed against him at the police station.

headline_en: Attacks on foreigners in Kyrgyzstan, Bangladeshi students in panic
summary_en: After a clash on 13 May 2024 between a few locals and Egyptian medical students in Bishkek, locals began attacking foreigners, including Bangladeshi, Pakistani and Indian students and workers; Bangladeshi students told Prothom Alo they were hiding and wanted to go home. Bangladesh has no embassy in Kyrgyzstan; the embassy in Uzbekistan covers it, estimates 600-800 students and about a thousand workers there, and told students to stay indoors.

facts.statement: On 13 May 2024 two or three local residents clashed with some Egyptian medical university students in Bishkek; attacks on foreigners in Bishkek then began, which the article dates to the night of 16 May, while a student quoted says attacks began on the evening of Friday (17 May). Bangladeshi, Pakistani and Indian students were attacked, foreigners were beaten house to house, property was vandalised and attackers entered medical college hostels.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladeshi students and others, to Prothom Alo

facts.statement: The article says at least 800 Bangladeshi medical students are in Kyrgyzstan; the Bangladesh Embassy (in Uzbekistan) has no statistics on how many Bangladeshis are there but estimates 600 to 800 students and about a thousand workers.
facts.source_in_article: reporter; Bangladesh Embassy in Uzbekistan estimate

facts.statement: Bangladesh has no embassy in Kyrgyzstan; the Bangladesh Embassy in Uzbekistan is responsible for Kyrgyzstan. The ambassador said a number is kept open for round-the-clock contact with the embassy (the number is not printed).
facts.source_in_article: Ambassador to Uzbekistan Mohammad Monirul Islam

facts.statement: The embassy told Bangladeshi students in Kyrgyzstan not to leave their homes; the university authority (Royal Metropolitan Medical University, Bishkek) told students not to go outside their rooms.
facts.source_in_article: Ambassador Mohammad Monirul Islam; student Syed Rakibul Islam

facts.statement: Students said Bangladeshi workers and students were injured in the attacks, but no one could give a number; the ambassador said that as of 18 May 2024 there was no information of any Bangladeshi being injured or killed, and that Kyrgyzstan's foreign ministry said the situation was under control. (The two accounts differ.)
facts.source_in_article: Bangladeshi students; Ambassador Mohammad Monirul Islam

facts.statement: Bangladeshi students said social-media apps were being used to locate foreign students, locals were patrolling the city in convoys of 20-25 cars, students of various countries were hiding in groups of 15-20 in a room, and police deployed across the city failed to control the situation. There were also allegations of abuse of female foreign students.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladeshi students; videos sent by students

facts.statement: Third-year student Syed Rakibul Islam of Royal Metropolitan Medical University, Bishkek, said he had gone nearly two days without food while in hiding and wanted to return to Bangladesh; Saima Kabir, second-semester student at Kyrgyz State Medical Academy, said locals were attacking foreign students and workers, that her hostel was not safe with angry locals outside, and asked for security help.
facts.source_in_article: students Syed Rakibul Islam and Saima Kabir

headline_en: Five Bangladeshis including a woman honoured for sending remittance from Italy
summary_en: The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome gave its 'Remittance Award' on 2 April 2024 to five expatriates (four individuals including one woman, and one business) as the top remitters from Italy for July 2022 to June 2023. The event also covered government services for expatriates, the Universal Pension Scheme and legal-channel remittance initiatives.

facts.statement: On 2 April 2024 at 4:30 pm the Bangladesh Embassy in Rome held a ceremony giving 'Remittance Award' crests to five expatriate Bangladeshis, including one woman, to encourage sending remittance through legal channels.

The Rome embassy's 2023 Remittance Award went to the highest remittance senders from Italy to Bangladesh in July 2022 to June 2023: individual (male) category Uddin Zia, Md. Mahfuzul Haque and Md. Omar Faruk; individual (female) category Mehenas Tabbasum; institution category Nibash Chakraborty, proprietor of Kaf PC Point.

The Rome embassy event included discussion of Bangladesh government services and activities for expatriates, the benefits of the Universal Pension Scheme (Sarbajanin Pension Scheme) and simplification of its registration process, and government initiatives for legal-channel remittance.
Ambassador to Italy Md. Monirul Islam told expatriates in Italy that the embassy is working sincerely to solve passport-related problems and to raise the quality of other services.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome introduced the 'Remittance Award' in 2019 to encourage legal-channel remitters; the award ceremony could not be held on International Migrants Day (18 December) for unavoidable reasons and was held on 2 April 2024 instead.

headline_en: BGB has protested the border killings: Foreign Minister
summary_en: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud told reporters on 28 March 2024 that BGB had protested and held border meetings over two Bangladeshis shot dead by India's BSF at the Lalmonirhat and Naogaon borders on 25 and 26 March. Asked about worker recruitment in Malaysia, he said the embassy had been told to hold talks to resolve the workers' crisis and that talks with Malaysia's foreign minister and labour ministry were planned. He also spoke about the hijacked ship's sailors and Dr Yunus.

facts.statement: Asked on 28 March 2024 about worker recruitment in Malaysia, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said the Bangladesh embassy had been instructed to hold talks to resolve the workers' crisis, that Bangladesh had discussed it with the Malaysian ambassador in Dhaka, and that there was a plan to talk with Malaysia's foreign minister and labour ministry.
On the EU ban on importing Malaysian palm oil, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said there are many places to sell palm oil and that Bangladeshi workers would not be inconvenienced by it.

Two Bangladeshis were killed by fire from India's Border Security Force (BSF): one at the Lalmonirhat border on 25 March 2024 and one at the Naogaon border on 26 March 2024. BGB protested and held border meetings.

According to the foreign minister's account of the BSF version, at Lalmonirhat some Bangladeshis cut the barbed-wire fence and crossed into India; when challenged they surrounded BSF members, BSF fired and two were injured, one returned to Bangladesh and the other was admitted to hospital on the Indian side and later died. He said the Naogaon incident on 26 March was similar, caused by crossing into India.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud citing BSF

facts.statement: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said Bangladesh has long been discussing with India, including on his recent India visit, that non-lethal weapons be used at the border, and that such weapons are now used much more than before, so many people are injured by rubber bullets or pellets and return to Bangladesh.

On Bangladeshi sailors held hostage by Somali pirates, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said the government was in contact to free the sailors, was making multi-pronged efforts to rescue the ship and sailors safely, had 'come a long way', and that there was no food shortage on the ship.

headline_en: Three sentenced to life imprisonment in human trafficking case in Jhenaidah
summary_en: On 20 March 2024 the Human Trafficking Offences Prevention Tribunal in Jhenaidah sentenced three absconding accused from Maheshpur to rigorous life imprisonment. They had taken away a 13-year-old girl in December 2011 on the promise of sewing-machine work; her mother filed a case in May 2012 alleging she had been trafficked inside or outside the country.

facts.statement: On 20 March 2024 at about 11 am, Judge Mizanur Rahman of the Human Trafficking Offences Prevention Tribunal (Manob Pachar Oporadh Domon Tribunal) in Jhenaidah sentenced Rowshanara Begum, Chhanowar Hossain and Bappi Hossain of Nalpatua village, Maheshpur upazila, to rigorous life imprisonment in a human trafficking case. All three are absconding; the sentence takes effect from the day of arrest or surrender.

According to the case summary, the three accused visited a family in Sonardari village, Jhenaidah Sadar, through a family acquaintance and repeatedly offered to arrange sewing-machine work for the family's 13-year-old daughter. On the morning of 28 December 2011 the girl's mother handed her over in front of some local people; the mother had contact with the girl for three months, then contact was cut and the accused stalled when asked to return her.

After the accused refused to return the girl on 13 May 2012, the mother filed a case under the human trafficking law at Jhenaidah Sadar police station on 31 May 2012 alleging the girl had been trafficked within the country or abroad. Police filed the charge sheet on 20 July 2012; the verdict came on 20 March 2024.

headline_en: Make a list of those conspiring against the country from abroad: Foreign Minister to expatriates
summary_en: At a reception by Bangladeshi expatriates in Abu Dhabi on 9 March 2024, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud asked expatriates to list people who conspire and spread propaganda against the country from abroad and urged them to remit through legal channels. Expatriates raised demands on Bangladeshi schools, an education quota, passports, remittance subsidy and Wage Earners' Bond problems.

facts.statement: At a reception by UAE-based Bangladeshis at an Abu Dhabi hotel on Saturday 9 March 2024 at about 9:30 pm local time, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud called on expatriates to make a list of those who conspire, spread propaganda and vilify the country from abroad, saying the government is determined to take appropriate action against them, and said expatriates should refrain from activities against law and order abroad.
Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud urged expatriate Bangladeshis in the UAE to send remittance home through legal channels, saying it plays a big role in the economy.

Expatriates at the Abu Dhabi reception asked the foreign minister to intervene on: demands of the local Bangladeshi schools, an education quota in Bangladesh for expatriates' children, easier passport issuance and other services for expatriates in Bangladesh, recognition of remittance senders, a subsidy on sending remittance, and resolving complications with the Probashi Wage Earners' Bond.

headline_en: Export products must be diversified to capture the Malaysian market
summary_en: In an interview as Bangladesh and Malaysia began the first three-day round of free trade agreement (FTA) talks in Dhaka, Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber president Md. Anwar Shahid said the FTA can be concluded by the December 2027 deadline set by the two heads of government. He said easing manpower export to Malaysia must be part of the FTA talks and that Bangladesh should train skilled people for technology and higher-value services.

facts.statement: Bangladesh and Malaysia have started negotiations on a free trade agreement (FTA); the first round, lasting three days, was under way at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in Dhaka in late October 2026, and the two heads of government have set December 2027 as the deadline to complete the agreement.
facts.source_in_article: reporter; Md. Anwar Shahid, president, Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber of Commerce and Industry

facts.statement: Md. Anwar Shahid, president of the Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said easing manpower export to Malaysia must be included in the FTA talks; Bangladeshis going abroad are still mainly in low-skill work, and raising their skills for technology and other high-value services would raise income.

Anwar Shahid said manpower export is usually thought of as construction or plantation workers, but there is scope in technology and skill-based work such as semiconductor design; if trained, even a few hundred such workers abroad could bring significant income, so training must match market demand.

Anwar Shahid said Bangladesh has started moving quickly on trade agreement talks with 10 to 12 countries because it will lose trade benefits after LDC graduation; Malaysia has FTAs with 14 countries including India and Pakistan; and four-five or even six-seven meetings may be needed for the Malaysia talks.

headline_en: Shahed's body handed over to family, to be buried at village home in Bogura
summary_en: The body of Bangladeshi worker Shahed Ahmmed, killed in a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 10 October 2026, arrived in Dhaka on Friday 23 October 2026 and was handed to his wife in the presence of the state minister for foreign affairs. Two Bangladeshis died in that attack, and the state minister said three Bangladeshis had been killed in missile attacks in Saudi Arabia in the past month, with only Shahed's body returned so far.

facts.statement: On 10 October 2026 Bangladeshi worker Shahed Ahmmed of Madla village, Shajahanpur upazila, Bogura, was killed in an attack by the armed group Houthis on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Two Bangladeshis died in that attack; the other was Nasrullah Badarpuri of Nangalkot upazila, Cumilla.

Shahed Ahmmed worked as a plumber on the Jeddah project of a Saudi contracting firm and had a work permit (iqama); he was returning to his workplace in Jeddah via Riyadh after a one-month leave in Bangladesh and was at Riyadh airport when it was attacked.

Shahed Ahmmed's body reached Dhaka and was handed over to his wife Kohinur Akter at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on the morning of Friday 23 October 2026, 13 days after his death, in the presence of State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam; the family left for Bogura in a hearse.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said on 23 October 2026 that three Bangladeshis had been killed in missile attacks in Saudi Arabia in the past month; only Shahed's body had come home so far and efforts were under way to bring back the others quickly.

headline_en: Going abroad for higher study: what you must know before packing your bags
summary_en: A pre-departure checklist for students going abroad for the first time: documents to carry, airline and luggage rules, clothes, medicines and electronics, and arrangements for arrival. It quotes Shafiqul Islam Shimul, founder and CEO of BD Expert Education Consultancy.

facts.statement: Students leaving for study abroad should carry passport, visa, air ticket, the university offer letter and admission papers; if needed also academic certificates, transcripts, scholarship papers, proof of financial capacity and accommodation details, and should check in advance whether the destination country requires health-related or other documents.

Keep originals safe, make several sets of photocopies and digital copies, and keep important documents in hand luggage rather than checked luggage; check passport and visa validity, ticket date, flight time, and that the name on the ticket matches the passport.

For international flights the usual advice is to reach the airport at least three hours before departure, but the airline's instructions should be followed; find out beforehand whether the flight is direct or has a transit, whether a change of aircraft is needed and whether there is enough time for the next flight.

Luggage weight and size limits differ by airline, so check the baggage policy given with the ticket, what is allowed in hand luggage, the limit on liquids and which items are banned; carrying banned or restricted items can cause trouble at the airport.

Shafiqul Islam Shimul, founder and CEO of BD Expert Education Consultancy, said passport, necessary medicines and valuables should be in hand luggage, and that accommodation, transport and emergency contacts should be arranged before arriving abroad.
facts.source_in_article: Shafiqul Islam Shimul, BD Expert Education Consultancy

facts.statement: Regular medicines should be carried in their original packets; for prescription medicines carry the doctor's prescription and check the destination country's rules on carrying medicines. Choose clothes for the destination's weather and avoid overloading luggage.

Pack phone, laptop, chargers, cables and a power adapter and check that devices are compatible with the destination country's sockets and voltage; keep digital copies of important files on the phone or secure online storage.

Before travel, fix where you will stay, how you will get from the airport to accommodation and whom to contact in an emergency; save contacts of the university's international student support office, the housing authority and acquaintances; learn the local emergency number; and have phone internet and necessary cash or an internationally usable card ready.

headline_en: Why did the MP who said 'corpse of sin' make a U-turn
summary_en: An opinion column on the execution (beheading) of two Bangladeshi citizens in Saudi Arabia, which Bangladeshi authorities say they learned of only from media reports. It criticises the state minister for foreign affairs for calling it a 'lesson' and saying little can be done, a BNP MP for saying he did not want the 'corpse of sin' brought home (later withdrawn with an apology), and opposition parties' silence, and argues embassies must ensure lawyers, consular contact, appeals and clemency pleas.

facts.statement: Two Bangladeshi citizens were tried, sentenced to death and executed (an MP's post describes it as beheading) in Saudi Arabia; Bangladeshi authorities say they knew nothing beforehand and learned of it after media reports. Full details of the charges and trial had not been published as of 19 October 2026.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said the execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia 'is a big lesson for us' and that 'when something happens under their law, there is not much for us to do' (quoted from Prothom Alo online and Bangla Tribune, 17 October 2026).
facts.source_in_article: State Minister Shama Obaed Islam, as quoted by the columnist

facts.statement: On 18 October 2026 Bangladesh's Ministry of Foreign Affairs called in the Saudi ambassador and asked for detailed information about the executions; a ministry official described it as a meeting rather than a 'summons'.

The columnist argues that when a citizen is arrested abroad, embassies must work to ensure he gets a lawyer, understands the charges and can state his case; Bangladesh cannot change a foreign court's verdict but can help appoint a lawyer, maintain consular contact, and pursue appeal and a plea to commute the sentence.

The column says a Sri Lankan citizen was recently sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia in a blasphemy case; the Sri Lankan government took diplomatic and legal steps, a special lawyers' team worked with Saudi lawyers, and the Saudi Supreme Court later overturned the death sentence.

BNP MP Kamruzzaman Ratan said on a Star News talk show that he would never hope for 'this corpse of sin' to come to Bangladesh, referring to the bodies of the two executed Bangladeshis; he later withdrew the remark fully in a Facebook post and apologised to the families and to expatriates.
facts.source_in_article: columnist quoting the MP's talk-show remarks and Facebook post

facts.statement: As of the writing of the column, no formal reaction to the executions had been received from Jamaat-e-Islami or NCP.

summary_en: Remittance received through BRAC Bank passed USD 2.5 billion (250 crore) in the first nine months of 2026, beating its 2025 record of USD 2.2 billion; the bank targets over USD 3 billion by year-end. The article lists the bank's products for expatriates and their families.

facts.statement: Remittance coming through BRAC Bank exceeded USD 250 crore (2.5 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, surpassing its 2025 record of USD 220 crore; the bank has set a target of more than USD 300 crore by the end of 2026.
BRAC Bank offers expatriates and their families a Probashi Virtual Savings Account, Probashi Poribar Account, TARA Probashi Poribar Account and Offshore Banking Unit services.
Expatriates can open a BRAC Bank account from abroad through the bank's digital e-KYC platform, and use the 'Astha' app for fund transfer, bill payment and opening DPS and FDR.

BRAC Bank has built a network with exchange houses in the Middle East, South-East Asia, Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific corridors, with host-to-host integration and API connectivity with international partners, and delivers remittance through its branches, sub-branches and agent banking network including in rural areas.
BRAC Bank holds 'uthan boithok' (courtyard meetings) with remittance-receiving customers to raise awareness about sending remittance through legal channels and about banking services.

headline_en: Government gives Tk 1,000 crore to keep Janata Bank's UAE operations alive
summary_en: The government provided AED 30 crore (about USD 8.17 crore, roughly BDT 1,003 crore) in capital so state-owned Janata Bank's four UAE branches can keep operating after the UAE central bank ordered them wound up for failing to maintain paid-up capital. The branches serve Bangladeshi workers and expatriates with remittance, accounts and bond investment.

facts.statement: The Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance instructed Janata Bank to send USD 81,677,104 to the UAE by Wednesday 9 September 2026, a capital injection of AED 30 crore (USD 8.17 crore, about BDT 1,003 crore), so that Janata Bank's four UAE branches in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah and Al Ain can continue services.

Under UAE central bank rules Janata Bank should hold paid-up capital of AED 40 crore in the UAE but had AED 10 crore, a shortfall of AED 30 crore. The UAE central bank wrote to the bank several times in 2026; its latest letter set a deadline and asked for an administrator to be appointed to wind up operations, told branches to stop opening new customer accounts or offering any new service, and restricted withdrawals from Janata Bank's account at the UAE central bank.

Bangladeshis in the UAE can send remittance through Janata Bank's four UAE branches (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Al Ain) and open savings, current and term accounts; the branches also offer investment in the Wage Earners Development Bond and US Dollar Premium Bond, and open LCs, give commercial guarantees and commercial loans for Bangladesh-UAE trade.
Janata Bank has operated in the UAE since 1976; its services there are used by Bangladeshi workers and expatriate Bangladeshis.

headline_en: Family of banned Chhatra League leader Monirul, involved in attack on Badhon, lock house and leave village
summary_en: Monirul Hawlader (24) of Madaripur, an Italy-based leader of the banned Chhatra League, was reported involved in an attack on actress Azmeri Haque Badhon in Mestre near Venice on the night of 7 September 2026. After activists and intelligence personnel came to his village home on 8 September, his family locked the house and left. His stepbrother said Monirul went to Italy via Libya through a broker about a year and a half earlier for 28 lakh taka, and that the debt is still on his mother and brother.

facts.date: about early 2025 (a year and a half before September 2026)
facts.statement: Monirul Hawlader (24) of Khalanikandi, Dhurail union, Madaripur Sadar, travelled to Italy via Libya through a broker (dalal) about a year and a half before September 2026, paying 28 lakh taka, according to his stepbrother Obaidul Hawlader.

The 28 lakh taka paid for Monirul Hawlader's Libya-to-Italy journey left a debt that still rests on his mother and elder brother; he has not been able to build a house at the village home, where the family has two dilapidated tin-shed rooms.

After Monirul Hawlader was reported involved in an attack on and harassment of actress Azmeri Haque Badhon at a park in Mestre, Italy, on the night of Monday 7 September 2026, people including local Anti-Discrimination Student Movement and National Citizen Party activists and intelligence personnel came to his Madaripur home on 8 September; the family locked the house and fled.

Madaripur Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Sadar Circle) Fariha Rafiq said that since the incident happened abroad, action against Monirul would be taken under that country's law, and that police were alert so nobody could attack the family's home.

Monirul was organising secretary of the banned Chhatra League's Dhurail union unit and left Bangladesh after the mass uprising of 2024; the union parishad chairman said he has heard Monirul still does Chhatra League politics from abroad.

headline_en: Told his wife 'I got a promotion'; died in explosion in Russia before the month ended
summary_en: Zakir Hossain of Bhairab, Kishoreganj, was among 15 people killed in an explosion at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia in late August 2026. He had gone to Russia on 4 February 2025 at a cost of 7 lakh taka raised by selling land and borrowing, earned about BDT 60,000 a month, and about 1.5 lakh taka of debt remains. The family is waiting for his body; the UNO promised efforts to bring it back and is considering financial help.

facts.statement: An explosion at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia on a Tuesday (about 25 August 2026) killed 15 people, including Bangladeshi worker Zakir Hossain of Atkapara village, Kalikaprasad union, Bhairab upazila, Kishoreganj; his body was recovered on the following Thursday. A linked headline says one Bangladeshi worker was killed and another was missing.

Zakir Hossain was sent to Russia on 4 February 2025 at a cost of 7 lakh taka: 4 lakh from selling land, 2 lakh as a loan from an NGO, and the rest also borrowed. About 1.5 lakh taka of debt is still outstanding.

Zakir Hossain's job was at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia with a salary of about BDT 60,000 (in Bangladeshi currency); after his own costs he could not send much home and what he sent went to repaying loans. He had been promoted less than a month before his death and told his wife his pay would rise.

Bhairab Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) K M Mamunur Rashid said the administration will make every effort to bring Zakir Hossain's body home and is considering whether the poor family can be given financial assistance. The family learned of the death on Friday from his cousin Ali Hossain, who lived with him in Russia.

headline_en: Dollar price in open market Tk 126.50
summary_en: On Monday 24 August 2026 the Money Changers Association of Bangladesh (MCAB) announced an open-market dollar rate: buying at BDT 125.50 and selling at BDT 126.50, after the rate had recently risen to BDT 128 and Bangladesh Bank tightened supervision. MCAB's president said money changers deal only in cash foreign currency, mainly from returning passengers and migrant workers, and cannot bring in remittance directly.

facts.statement: From 24 August 2026 money exchanges in Bangladesh are to buy US dollars at BDT 125.50 and sell at BDT 126.50 (BDT 1 more), under a rate announced by the Money Changers Association of Bangladesh (MCAB); the open-market rate had recently risen to BDT 128 and Bangladesh Bank had stepped up supervision of money changers.

MCAB president M S Zaman said money changers only buy and sell cash foreign currency, do not transact electronic or virtual currency and cannot bring in remittance directly; cash foreign currency brought by returning passengers and migrant workers is the main source of their business.
MCAB communicates the dollar rate to all money changers in the country through the association's website.

MCAB's president blamed banks, not money changers, for manipulation in the dollar market and demanded clear instructions for money changers, more scope for legal dollar transactions and easier policy to shut the illegal market.

headline_en: Expatriate Bangladeshi singer Sohel Rana at 'National Day' event on invitation of Singapore government
summary_en: Sohel Rana, a work-permit holder and singer of the 'Migrants Band Singapore', was invited by the Singapore government to the country's 61st National Day event at Kallang National Stadium on 9 August 2026 and was shown on the stadium screen and national TV wearing the Bangladesh flag. The band was started by migrant workers 15 years ago.

facts.statement: The Singapore government invited Sohel Rana, a Bangladeshi migrant worker and singer of 'Migrants Band Singapore', to the 61st National Day event at Kallang National Stadium on 9 August 2026, the only expatriate Bangladeshi invited; he said that as a work-permit-holding temporary resident he was proud, because normally only a limited number of Singaporeans get to attend.

'Migrants Band Singapore' was started in Singapore 15 years ago by a group of young art-minded migrants; current regular members include Nilsagar Shahin, Sohel Rana, Ujjal Kumar, Sajib Saha and others.

headline_en: Mamun, arrested at airport on allegation of involvement in extremism, remanded for 3 days
summary_en: Md. Mamun Hossain (26) of Munshiganj was detained at Dhaka airport's immigration at about 1:30 am on 20 July 2026 while, by his account, leaving for Qatar on a labour visa, and was remanded for three days on allegations of links to an extremist organisation. He said he is on bail in two anti-terrorism cases and no court barred him from travelling; the judge asked whether he had taken court permission to go abroad. The prosecution said he went to France via Portugal in 2020 and was sent back that year over alleged extremist activity.

facts.statement: Md. Mamun Hossain (26) of Dakshin Paikpara, Tongibari upazila, Munshiganj, was detained at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at about 1:30 am on the night of Sunday into Monday 20 July 2026; CTTC arrested him from the immigration detention room on intelligence about links to an extremist organisation and seized his passport, mobile phones and belongings. He told the court he was going to Qatar on a labour visa.

In court Mamun said two Anti-Terrorism Act cases against him are under trial but he is on bail in both and no court had prohibited him from going abroad; the Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate (Md. Jewel Rana) responded: 'You have misused the law. Did you take any permission from the court to go abroad?'

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md. Jewel Rana rejected bail and granted three days' remand for Mamun Hossain on 20 July 2026; the investigating officer, CTTC SI Md. Motiur Rahman Molla, had shown him arrested under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and sought seven days.
facts.source_in_article: state lawyer Harun Or Rashid; court

facts.statement: The prosecution said Mamun went from Bangladesh to France via Portugal in 2020 and was sent back the same year on allegations of involvement in extremist activity, and was arrested on return; in 2024 he was arrested in another anti-terrorism case and gave a statement in court. Mamun claimed that in 2019 he was picked up at the airport while going abroad, held disappeared for 20 days, then shown arrested in a Gendaria police station case and forced to give a statement.
facts.source_in_article: state lawyer Harun Or Rashid; Mamun in court

headline_en: Returned from abroad does not mean expatriate: the reality behind the label
summary_en: An opinion piece by the president of Bangladesh Press Club, Kuwait, objecting to news reports that label people caught at Bangladesh's airports with gold, mobile phones or other goods evading customs duty as 'expatriates' without verification. He asks media and customs officials to check length of stay abroad, visa type and residency before using the label.

facts.statement: Moin Uddin Sarkar Sumon, president of Bangladesh Press Club, Kuwait, writes that people detained at Bangladesh's airports for customs evasion with gold, mobile phones or other goods are often called 'expatriates' in news without verification, which harms the image of Bangladeshis working legally abroad.

The writer says before identifying a detained returnee as an expatriate, media, authorities and customs officials should verify how long the person stayed abroad, what type of visa they held (worker, business, student or tourist), whether their residency was valid, and whether they were a long-term expatriate at all.

headline_en: Diplomacy of national interest and Bangladesh's new journey
summary_en: An opinion column by a migration professor at Universiti Brunei Darussalam arguing for multi-directional, interest-based diplomacy. It says Malaysia matters for Bangladesh's labour market, expatriate welfare and skill export, that the lives and income of lakhs of Bangladeshi workers depend on that relationship, and that government-to-government talks cover lowering recruitment costs, easing visas and protecting migrants.

facts.statement: Columnist Dr A K M Ahsan Ullah (professor of international, security and migration studies, Universiti Brunei Darussalam) writes that the lives, income, dignity and safety of lakhs of Bangladeshi workers depend on relations with Malaysia, so high-level talks with Malaysia are diplomacy tied to people's livelihoods, not a symbolic visit.
facts.source_in_article: columnist Dr A K M Ahsan Ullah

facts.statement: The columnist lists as part of government-to-government talks: whether recruitment costs in labour markets can be reduced, whether visas can be eased, whether migrants' protection can be ensured, and whether student and research exchange can be increased.
facts.source_in_article: columnist Dr A K M Ahsan Ullah

headline_en: A new template of multi-directional diplomacy: significance of the Prime Minister's three visits
summary_en: An opinion piece by the Prime Minister's deputy press secretary on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's June 2026 visits to Malaysia, the Summer Davos in Dalian and Beijing. In Putrajaya on 22 June he asked Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to consider regularising Bangladeshis who had become irregular and renewing work permits, and requested recruitment of skilled workers; with Kazakhstan's prime minister he discussed sending skilled workers to Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: At a meeting at the Prime Minister's Office in Putrajaya on 22 June 2026 (10 am local time), Prime Minister Tarique Rahman asked Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to consider regularising Bangladeshi nationals who had become irregular for various reasons and renewing their work permits, and requested the Malaysian government to recruit skilled workers from Bangladesh. The article reports the request, not a decision by Malaysia.
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

facts.statement: The Bangladesh-Malaysia prime ministers' talks covered the free trade agreement (FTA), halal economy, semiconductors, higher education, vocational training, tourism, energy, defence, AI, digital economy, cyber security and modern technology; a joint statement of 33 points on 9 areas of cooperation was issued. The visit lasted 18 hours.
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

facts.statement: On the sidelines of the World Economic Forum's 17th 'Summer Davos' in Dalian, China, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a bilateral meeting with Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov that discussed setting up permanent diplomatic missions in Dhaka and Astana and sending skilled workers from Bangladesh to Kazakhstan, along with energy, digital infrastructure and technology cooperation.
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

facts.statement: In Beijing, Bangladesh and China signed 17 memoranda of understanding (13 at ministry level, 3 between BIDA and Chinese organisations, 1 between BNP and the Communist Party of China); representatives of at least 12 Chinese companies made investment proposals said to total more than USD 900 crore (about BDT 1 lakh 10 thousand crore).
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

headline_en: PM's Malaysia visit opens new prospects for future cooperation between the two countries: Mahdi Amin
summary_en: On his first foreign visit as Prime Minister, Tarique Rahman met Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim on 22 June 2026 and called for the Malaysian labour market to be reopened quickly to Bangladeshi workers, with lower migration cost and safe workplaces. The two sides also discussed regularising or safely returning irregular and jailed Bangladeshis in Malaysia. A 33-point joint statement on nine areas of cooperation was issued.

facts.statement: As of 22 June 2026 the Malaysian labour market was not open to Bangladeshi workers: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, visiting Malaysia, called on Malaysia to quickly reopen ('quickly open up') its labour market for Bangladeshi workers.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

facts.statement: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman asked Malaysia to create employment opportunities for more Bangladeshi workers at low cost and through a transparent process, and called for lower migration cost and a safe working environment.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

facts.statement: At the Bangladesh-Malaysia prime ministers' meeting on 22 June 2026 the two sides discussed humanely regularising (giving legal status to) Bangladeshis who are in irregular status or in prison in Malaysia, or returning them safely to Bangladesh. The article reports discussion only, not a decision.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

facts.statement: Tarique Rahman's visit to Malaysia was his first foreign trip since taking office and lasted about 18 hours; he met Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim (first one-to-one, then at delegation level) and the King, Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

facts.statement: The Bangladesh-Malaysia talks covered political cooperation, trade and investment, halal industry, digital economy, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, the labour market, education, tourism, energy, defence and security; a 33-point joint statement was issued to increase cooperation on nine subjects.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

facts.statement: After arriving in Kuala Lumpur, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held an exchange of views with expatriate Bangladeshis, presented his plans for Bangladesh and recalled expatriates' contribution to the country's development.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

facts.statement: Bangladesh and Malaysia agreed to take forward talks on a free trade agreement (FTA), and discussed Malaysian investment in Bangladesh's technology parks and economic zones and cooperation on halal certification, research, training and creating skilled manpower.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

facts.statement: During the visit one memorandum of understanding on culture was signed and two 'exchange of notes' (on increasing investment and on counter-terrorism) were exchanged; Bangladesh sought Malaysia's support on Rohingya repatriation, on becoming an ASEAN sectoral dialogue partner and on joining RCEP. Top officials of Petronas, Axiata, AirAsia, Perodua and MMC Port met the Prime Minister.
facts.source_in_article: Mahdi Amin, adviser to the Prime Minister and spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office, at a press conference at the Shangri-La hotel in Malaysia on 22 June 2026

headline_en: Five young men from Sylhet killed in road accident in Qatar
summary_en: Five Bangladeshi workers from Kanaighat upazila, Sylhet, died on the morning of 21 June 2026 in the Sanaiya area of Qatar when the pickup van taking them to work went out of control. The State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare said the labour wing of the Bangladesh embassy in Qatar has been instructed to bring the bodies home quickly and arrange due financial compensation for the families.

facts.statement: Five Bangladeshi workers from Kanaighat upazila, Sylhet, were killed on the spot on the morning of Sunday 21 June 2026 in the Sanaiya area of Qatar when the pickup van carrying them to their workplace went out of control.
facts.source_in_article: Relatives of the dead; death confirmed by Kanaighat UNO Mehedi Hasan Shakil

facts.statement: The five dead in the Qatar accident were named as Mostak Ahmad (30), son of Salim Ullah, and Zubayer Ahmad (30), son of the late Ahsan Ullah, both of Majhtaluk village, Jhingabari union; Jasim Uddin (30), son of Siraj Uddin, of Agtaluk village; Jibal Ahmad (36), son of Abdun Nur, of Amarpur village; and Kadir Ahmad (24), son of Bahar Uddin, of Gachhbari Noyagram, Dakshin Banigram union, all in Kanaighat upazila, Sylhet.
facts.source_in_article: Abdul Latif, member of Jhingabari Union Parishad

facts.statement: The bodies of the five Bangladeshis killed in the Qatar road accident were kept in the morgue of a local hospital in Qatar; families in Bangladesh learned of the deaths at about 12 noon the same day.

The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment instructed the labour wing of the Bangladesh embassy in Qatar to work with the highest priority to bring the five bodies home quickly and to provide due financial compensation to the affected families. No amount is stated.

headline_en: Shakil wanted release from a Saudi jail; he came home a lifeless body
summary_en: The body of Shakil Mia (28) of Kishoreganj, who died in a Saudi prison on 15 May 2026, reached his home on 13 June 2026, 28 days after his death, brought back at government initiative. He had gone to Saudi Arabia in 2019 through a Banani recruiting agency, left his employer over an iqama problem, was arrested while working illegally, and the family sent about BDT 180,000 to a lawyer for bail before he died.

facts.statement: Shakil Mia of Kishoreganj went to Saudi Arabia in 2019, on borrowed money, through Altab Recruiting Agency (আলতাব রিক্রুটিং এজেন্সি) in the Banani area of Dhaka.
facts.source_in_article: Bakul Mia, uncle of the deceased

facts.statement: In Saudi Arabia Shakil Mia left his workplace because of complications with his employer over his work/residence permit (iqama); he was later caught by Saudi police while working illegally and sent to prison.
facts.source_in_article: Bakul Mia, uncle of the deceased

facts.statement: From a Saudi prison Shakil Mia told his family that about 2 lakh taka was needed to arrange bail so he could return home; his father says he borrowed and sent about BDT 180,000 to a lawyer in Saudi Arabia. The article gives both figures (about 2 lakh needed; about 1 lakh 80 thousand sent).

Shakil Mia (28) died on 15 May 2026 in a Saudi prison; relatives claim an air conditioner exploded in the prison, creating smoke, and he developed breathing difficulty and died there. He had earlier told family by phone that he was weak, had lost weight and could not eat the prison food.
The father of a Bangladeshi who died in a Saudi prison said about 8,000 Saudi riyals were needed to bring the body from Saudi Arabia to Bangladesh, which the family did not have.
facts.source_in_article: Omar Faruk, father of the deceased

facts.statement: Shakil Mia's body was brought home at government initiative after Shariful Alam, MP for Kishoreganj-6 (Bhairab-Kuliarchar) and State Minister for Textiles and Jute, took it up; the body arrived on a Bangladesh Biman flight from Saudi Arabia at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka, at about midnight on Friday 12 June 2026 and reached the home in Purba Katiarchar, Maria union, Kishoreganj Sadar, on the morning of 13 June, 28 days after the death.
Shakil Mia was his family's only earner; the family last spoke to him 10 days before his death, when he asked for money for bail and legal process.

headline_en: India tries to push alleged undocumented Bangladeshis across the border; panic among Muslims in West Bengal
summary_en: An Al Jazeera feature reports that the newly elected BJP government of West Bengal has since late May 2026 been detaining alleged undocumented Bangladeshi Muslim migrants and trying to push them into Bangladesh under a 'detect, delete and deport' policy, with temporary detention centres in every district. Bangladeshi families who had crossed with brokers to work in Kolkata describe surrendering or leaving out of fear. Dhaka has protested and BGB says it blocked at least 18 push-in attempts since 4 June.

facts.statement: In late May 2026 West Bengal's newly elected BJP chief minister Suvendu Adhikari ordered alleged Bangladeshi migrants living illegally in the state to be sent back, under a state 'detect, delete and deport' policy; the state also announced building 'holding centres' to detain alleged illegal Bangladeshis before return. The BJP had come to power in West Bengal for the first time about a month before mid-June 2026.
facts.source_in_article: Al Jazeera report carried by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said the drive would be conducted only against Muslim Bangladeshis; Hindu and other-faith migrants are excluded under a disputed constitutional amendment (as the article words it). He also said detainees need not be taken to court before expulsion.
facts.source_in_article: Al Jazeera report carried by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: In December 2025 India's Supreme Court ruled that foreign nationals have almost no rights under the Indian constitution; as a result, under the West Bengal policy people facing expulsion have to prove why they should not be sent to Bangladesh.
facts.source_in_article: Al Jazeera report carried by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: In the two weeks to about 13 June 2026 thousands of people were detained across West Bengal; some were sent to detention centres and others taken to the border in attempts to push them into Bangladesh.
facts.source_in_article: Al Jazeera report carried by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: On Sunday 7 June 2026 West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari claimed about 5,000 Bangladeshi nationals had already been sent back; in his own words 4,800 'Bangladeshi infiltrators' had been returned from the centres and 836 more were in detention centres awaiting quick return. He said temporary detention centres had been set up in every district of the state.
facts.source_in_article: Suvendu Adhikari, to journalists in Kolkata

facts.statement: A police officer on duty at Hakimpur border checkpost (North 24 Parganas, about 80 km from Kolkata) claimed 250 to 300 undocumented migrants and refugees arrive there (are brought to the border detention centre) every day; their citizenship is checked and biometric data collected to build a digital list of migrants. Crowds have been seen at Hakimpur and other West Bengal border posts since late May 2026.
facts.source_in_article: Unnamed police officer at Hakimpur, to Al Jazeera

facts.statement: Raisul Islam (38) of Satkhira said he paid a broker about USD 250 (about BDT 30,700 at the rate given in the article) to get himself and his family across the border into India two years earlier.

Raisul Islam and his wife both worked as masons on the outskirts of Kolkata and together earned about USD 10 a day (about BDT 1,230); he said wages in India were higher than what he earned in Bangladesh.
Mirajul Gazi (42) and his wife worked as construction labourers in Kolkata and earned about USD 12 a day (about BDT 1,470).

Raisul Islam said he and his family surrendered voluntarily before the authorities found them, fearing harassment by local people and police as illegal migrants; Indian security forces then took his family by vehicle to a detention centre 18 km from Hakimpur checkpost.

Mirajul Gazi said he had no problem for five years in Kolkata, but after the new government came to power his landlord told him to leave, and fearing attack by locals the family decided to return to Bangladesh.
Many migrants gathered at Hakimpur said economic hardship and lack of livelihood in Bangladesh forced them to cross the border into India with the help of brokers; many had no valid papers.
facts.source_in_article: Migrants at Hakimpur, to Al Jazeera

facts.statement: Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said that since 4 June 2026 it had blocked at least 18 'push-in' attempts by India's BSF, in which about 180 people were to be pushed into Bangladesh.

Bangladesh's State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed said at a Dhaka press conference (Monday, about 8 June 2026) that Dhaka had sent '12 to 13 letters' to Delhi on the matter, that there is a set mechanism for verifying nationality of undocumented migrants which Indian authorities must follow, and that the drive could affect bilateral relations.
At the 57th BGB-BSF director-general-level border conference in Delhi (started Monday, ended Thursday, about 8-11 June 2026) BGB called for an end to 'push-ins' into Bangladesh.
facts.source_in_article: Al Jazeera report carried by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: India's foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal claimed illegal foreigners are being dealt with under Indian law, that Bangladesh and other countries were informed for verification, and that many such requests are still pending verification by Dhaka; according to media reports India's foreign ministry has sent details of more than 2,800 suspected Bangladeshis to Dhaka.

In summer 2025 Indian security agencies in Assam accused about 12 Indian Muslims of being undocumented migrants and forced them across the border into Bangladesh; Bangladesh sent them back, they were stranded for a time in no man's land and were finally taken back into India, without explanation or redress.
facts.source_in_article: Al Jazeera report carried by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: Human Rights Watch Asia director Elaine Pearson said detainees should have the right to legal aid even without valid papers, so that no Indian citizen is wrongly expelled, and called the process 'illegal'. Activist Teesta Setalvad said police are indiscriminately picking people up and sending them to detention centres and demanded full disclosure of data on those detained and expelled.
facts.source_in_article: Elaine Pearson (HRW) and Teesta Setalvad, to Al Jazeera

facts.statement: Bangladesh and India share a 4,096 km land border; West Bengal has about 100 million people, about 27 percent of them Muslim.
facts.source_in_article: Al Jazeera report carried by Prothom Alo

headline_en: Various facilities announced for the service sector
summary_en: A report on the proposed FY 2026-27 budget's service-sector measures. For migrants, the budget announces a 'Probashi Card' for outbound and working expatriates to store worker data and ease access to government services and welfare benefits, and stresses new labour markets, skills, easy-term loans and safe migration. It also proposes a single ID for all services and a student education loan programme.

facts.statement: The proposed FY 2026-27 budget announces the launch of a 'Probashi Card' (প্রবাসী কার্ড) for people going abroad and expatriates working abroad; through the card, workers' information will be stored and the process of taking various government services and getting welfare benefits will be made easier. No launch date, fee or issuing office is stated.
facts.source_in_article: Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, proposed budget for FY 2026-27

facts.statement: The proposed FY 2026-27 budget puts emphasis on exploring new labour markets, skills development, loans on easy terms and a safe migration system for migrant workers; the article gives no amounts or terms.
facts.source_in_article: Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, proposed budget for FY 2026-27

facts.statement: The proposed FY 2026-27 budget seeks to encourage migration, transport and government-service digitalisation through tax and VAT exemptions (no detail given).

The budget proposes a single ID through which all government and private services can be taken, and strengthening Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) so that government services, fee payment, registration and information verification can be done on one digital platform.
facts.source_in_article: Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, proposed budget for FY 2026-27

facts.statement: The budget proposes an education loan programme for students so that financial limits do not keep anyone from higher education or technical training.
facts.source_in_article: Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, proposed budget for FY 2026-27

headline_en: Nearly 2.5 billion dollars in remittances came in just 19 days
summary_en: Ahead of Eid-ul-Azha, Bangladeshis abroad sent USD 2,483 million in the first 19 days of May 2026, 38 percent more than the same period a year earlier, according to Bangladesh Bank. Fiscal-year remittances from July to 19 May reached USD 31,816 million, and the central bank is buying surplus dollars from banks.

facts.statement: Remittances to Bangladesh in the first 19 days of May 2026 were USD 248 crore 30 lakh (USD 2,483 million), against USD 179 crore 30 lakh in the same period of the previous year, a rise of 38 percent.
From July of the current fiscal year to 19 May 2026, Bangladesh received USD 3,181 crore 60 lakh (USD 31,816 million) in remittances.
Bank officials said expatriates were sending more money ahead of Eid-ul-Azha (Qurbani Eid) and that at this pace May 2026 remittances could exceed USD 3 billion before Eid.
Because higher remittances created a dollar surplus in banks, Bangladesh Bank has been buying dollars to build reserves; on 20 May 2026 it bought USD 7 crore from four banks at BDT 122.75 per dollar.

headline_en: BMET to take 50 language trainers at BDT 800 an hour; applications close 20 April
summary_en: BMET is recruiting 50 guest language trainers to run language courses at government Technical Training Centres (TTCs) in Japanese, Russian, French and Italian. The notice shows which languages TTCs are staffing for and the qualification levels required of trainers; applications by post to BMET, Kakrail, by 20 April 2026, with exams on 24 April.

facts.statement: The Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) is recruiting 50 guest language trainers (a panel) to run language courses at government Technical Training Centres (TTCs): Japanese 40, Italian 6, Russian 2 and French 2.

Required qualification for BMET guest language trainers at TTCs: Japanese, at least HSC plus JLPT N3 or equivalent; Russian and French, a pass at Level B1 or equivalent in a language proficiency test; Italian, at least Level A2. Priority goes to people who stayed more than three years in the country concerned or served over a year as a language trainer at a reputed institution (the article's wording omits the number of years).
BMET guest language trainers at TTCs get an honorarium of BDT 800 per hour, payable for at most 4 hours a day.

To apply as a BMET guest language trainer: download the prescribed form from the BMET website, fill it in, send a scanned copy online and post the original application with attested copies of all educational and experience certificates to Director General, Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), 89/2, Kakrail, Dhaka. No applications are accepted in person. Deadline 20 April 2026.

Written and oral exams for all four languages (Japanese, Russian, French, Italian) for the BMET trainer panel are on 24 April 2026 at Dhaka Technical Teachers Training Institute (DTTTI), Mirpur, Dhaka.
BMET head office address as printed: Director General, Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), 89/2, Kakrail, Dhaka.

headline_en: Masud Uddin Chowdhury shown arrested in a Paltan police station human trafficking case: DB
summary_en: Former army officer and former MP Masud Uddin Chowdhury was arrested in Baridhara, Dhaka, on the night of 23 March 2026 and shown arrested in a human trafficking case at Paltan police station. Police say he faces 11 cases in all (6 in Feni, 5 in Dhaka), including murder, attempted murder and human trafficking, plus complaints under investigation at the ACC and CID. The article does not describe the trafficking allegations.

facts.statement: Masud Uddin Chowdhury, former lieutenant general and former Jatiya Party MP for Feni-3, was arrested from Baridhara, Dhaka, on the night of Monday 23 March 2026 and on 24 March was shown arrested in a case at Paltan police station filed on human trafficking allegations and sent to court.
facts.source_in_article: Shafiqul Islam, Additional Commissioner (DB chief), Dhaka Metropolitan Police, at a press conference on 24 March 2026

facts.statement: Police say there are 11 cases against Masud Uddin Chowdhury: 6 in Feni district and 5 in Dhaka metropolitan area (Paltan, Banani, Kotwali, Mirpur and Hatirjheel police stations) on charges including murder, attempted murder and human trafficking. Three Feni cases are under trial; he was absconding and courts had issued arrest warrants. Several complaints against him are also under investigation at the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) and police CID.
facts.source_in_article: Shafiqul Islam, Additional Commissioner (DB chief), Dhaka Metropolitan Police, at a press conference on 24 March 2026

facts.statement: Background of Masud Uddin Chowdhury as given: GOC of the army's 9th Division in 2007 and a key figure in the 1/11 changeover; coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on serious crimes; Bangladesh High Commissioner to Australia from 2008 with three extensions; after retirement involved in several businesses in Dhaka including restaurants; Jatiya Party MP for Feni-3 (Sonagazi-Daganbhuiyan) in 2018 and 2024. The article does not say what the human trafficking case alleges.

headline_en: Relatives wait for the body of a Bangladeshi killed in a missile attack in Saudi Arabia
summary_en: Abdullah Al Mamun (35) of Gafargaon, Mymensingh, injured on 8 March 2026 in an Iranian missile strike on a labour camp in Saudi Arabia, died on 17 March 2026. His family is asking the government to bring the body home; local officials say efforts have begun through the Wage Earners' Welfare Board and that rehabilitation support for the family is being planned.

facts.statement: On 8 March 2026, just before iftar, an Iranian missile strike hit a labour camp of Al Towaiq Baladia company (আল তোয়াইক বলদিয়া কোম্পানি) in Al Kharij city (আল খারিজ, as printed), Saudi Arabia, seriously injuring Bangladeshi worker Abdullah Al Mamun (35).

Abdullah Al Mamun (35), of Bharbhara village, Rasulpur union, Gafargaon, Mymensingh, who was on life support in hospital in Saudi Arabia after the missile strike, was declared dead at about 11:30 pm local time on Tuesday 17 March 2026; the family got the news on Wednesday 18 March.

Abdullah Al Mamun went to Saudi Arabia 15 years ago, last visited Bangladesh five years ago and was due to return home a month after Eid-ul-Fitr 2026 to build a new house; he leaves a wife, Sharmin Akter (30), and a son aged 6.

Gafargaon UNO N M Abdullah-Al-Mamun said efforts were being started through the Wage Earners' Welfare Board to bring the body of the Bangladeshi killed in the missile strike in Saudi Arabia home quickly, and that Eid-day supplies were being delivered to the family.

Mymensingh Deputy Commissioner Saifur Rahman said the UNO was instructed to give necessary support to the family of the Bangladeshi killed in the war and to plan how the family can be rehabilitated; after the body arrives and is buried, the administration will help with initiatives for the self-reliance of the wife and family. No amount is stated.

headline_en: 99 language trainer jobs at BMET, honorarium BDT 800 per hour
summary_en: BMET is recruiting 99 guest language trainers to run language courses at government Technical Training Centres (TTCs) in Japanese, Korean, Arabic, German, Italian and English. The notice shows which languages TTCs are staffing for and trainer qualifications; applications by post to BMET, Kakrail, by 18 March 2026, with exams on 3 and 10 April.

facts.statement: The Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) is recruiting 99 guest language trainers (a panel) to run language courses at government Technical Training Centres (TTCs): Japanese 50, English 20, Arabic 8, Italian 8, German 7 and Korean 6.

Required qualification for BMET guest language trainers at TTCs: for Japanese, Korean, German and Italian, at least HSC plus a specified level in the language (for example JLPT N3, TOPIK Level 3); for English and Arabic, a master's degree in the subject. Priority to people who have stayed in the country concerned or have experience.
BMET guest language trainers at TTCs get an honorarium of BDT 800 per hour, payable for at most 4 hours a day.

To apply as a BMET guest language trainer: download the prescribed form from the BMET website, fill it in, send a scanned copy online and post the original application with attested copies of all educational and experience certificates to Director General, Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), 89/2, Kakrail, Dhaka. No applications are accepted in person. Deadline 18 March 2026.

Written and oral exams for the BMET trainer panel: all languages except Japanese on 3 April 2026, Japanese on 10 April 2026, both at Dhaka Technical Teachers Training Institute (DTTTI), Mirpur, Dhaka.
BMET head office address as printed: Director General, Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), 89/2, Kakrail, Dhaka.

headline_en: Saleh last came to Moulvibazar four months ago
summary_en: Saleh Ahmad of Barlekha, Moulvibazar, who had lived in the UAE for 35 years and drove a water tanker in Ajman, was killed on the night of 28 February 2026 when an Iranian missile hit his vehicle. His two brothers in Ajman confirmed the death through his kafil (local sponsor/employer); the body is in a hospital there.

facts.statement: Saleh Ahmad (known abroad as Ahmad Ali) of Gazitekha (Banshtala) village, Barlekha upazila, Moulvibazar, was killed on Saturday 28 February 2026, some time after iftar, when a missile fired by Iran hit his vehicle in Ajman ('Ajman city of Dubai' as printed), UAE; he drove a water tanker and was out on the road delivering water.

Saleh Ahmad had lived in the UAE for 35 years; he visited Bangladesh last year and returned to Dubai about four months before his death. He last spoke to his wife by phone on Friday 27 February 2026. His wife, three sons and a daughter live in Bangladesh; two younger brothers, Zakir Hossain and Borhan Ahmad, also live in Ajman.

After the attack, military personnel took Saleh Ahmad to hospital; his two brothers went to the hospital in Ajman but were not allowed to see him, and they confirmed his death through the kafil (the local employer/sponsor). The body was being kept at the hospital. The family first heard at about 10 pm on Saturday.

headline_en: 263 people rescued while being trafficked to Malaysia in a wooden boat; 10 detained
summary_en: On the night of Saturday 3 January 2026 the Bangladesh Navy ship BNS Shadhinota chased and stopped a wooden boat 30 miles south-west of St Martin's Island, Cox's Bazar, rescuing 263 people including women and children who were being taken illegally by sea to Malaysia and detaining 10 members of a trafficking ring. The boat lacked life-saving gear, food and water; a case was being prepared at Teknaf police station.

facts.statement: On the night of Saturday 3 January 2026 the Bangladesh Navy rescued 263 people, including women and children, from a wooden boat 30 miles south-west of St Martin's Island, Cox's Bazar; those on board said they were trying to go to Malaysia illegally by sea.

Ten members of a trafficking ring were detained from the Malaysia-bound wooden boat; Navy ship BNS Shadhinota (বানৌজা স্বাধীনতা) signalled the boat to stop after noticing suspicious movement, the boat sped up to flee and was caught after a chase.

The Navy said the wooden boat used for the sea crossing to Malaysia had no minimum life-saving equipment, adequate food, water or safety arrangements, and that the voyage risked a humanitarian disaster in the deep sea.
The detained people and the seized boat were handed over to Teknaf police station; OC Saiful Islam said a human trafficking case was being prepared.
